questions.question: Do we have a verified record of what actually happened, or only of what was scheduled?
questions.have: 137 finals with scores, each carrying its official week-page URL, plus a 192-field reconciliation against the official standings page.
questions.lack: Anything after Week 10. The season is in progress, so the feed stops where the official pages stop.
questions.answer: YES for weeks 1-10, and it checks out: 192 of 192 club fields recompute exactly (32 clubs x W/L/T/PF/PA/games). This is the first time in this repository's history that a results feed exists at all.
questions.how_to_close: re-run the capture each week; nothing else is needed

questions.question: Does the rating we built actually predict games it has not seen?
questions.have: A walk-forward test on 89 games across weeks 4-10, with the parameters fixed before the run.
questions.lack: Any comparison to a market line, which is the only benchmark that matters.
questions.answer: Partly. The rating beats predicting a zero margin on MAE (9.29 vs 10.21 points) and gets 56 of 88 sides right (exact p=0.01375). That is a real signal about the score and NOT an edge over a price.
questions.how_to_close: the market comparison needs prices: Q-04

questions.question: Can we price a total at all, and is a normal approximation safe?
questions.have: A distribution measured on 137 games: totals mean 45.92 SD 14.26, |margin| mean 10.56 SD 7.91.
questions.lack: Pace, weather, and any adjustment for game script. The model total is a league average reshaped by a club pace proxy.
questions.answer: Yes, with a caveat: excess kurtosis is -0.146 for |margin| and 0.19 for the total, so a normal approximation is defensible but is an approximation. The backtest total MAE equals the naive fixed-total baseline, so the total is currently NOT better than a constant.
questions.how_to_close: a better total needs pace and situational inputs, not more data volume

questions.question: Can we obtain an official market price, opening and closing?
questions.have: A store with the schema, timestamps, invariants and provenance blocks, and our own line recorded in it.
questions.lack: Every market value. The NFL publishes no betting prices and no licensed feed is configured anywhere in this repository.
questions.answer: NO. 39 of 39 market cells are blank and flagged UNVERIFIED. Third-party prices exist in x3lab and are carried in their own columns as NOT OFFICIAL, deliberately unused.
questions.how_to_close: buy or license a price feed with open and close per market; this is a purchasing decision, not an engineering one

questions.question: If we had prices, would our line differ from the market enough to matter?
questions.have: Our own 13 Week-10 lines and a measured residual SD of 12.307 points for the model's error.
questions.lack: The market line. Without it the difference column is a column of blanks.
questions.answer: CANNOT BE ANSWERED. Any statement about 'a 1-point edge against the market' in this repository would be an assumption, not a measurement.
questions.how_to_close: same as Q-04; the difference column is already wired and will populate the day prices arrive

questions.question: May two legs of a parlay be multiplied as if independent?
questions.have: Two measured within-game coefficients on 137 finals.
questions.lack: Player-prop joint outcomes, and the same-game spread/team-total joint.
questions.answer: For a total and a margin: not shown to be dependent. r=-0.0157 with CI -0.1829 to 0.1524, permutation p=0.85281 - the interval contains zero, so multiplying is defensible for THESE two. For two teams' scores in one game, r=0.0759 (n=137, p=0.37953) - also no measurable dependence. Prop legs remain unmeasured and must not be multiplied.
questions.how_to_close: an official prop archive, which does not exist; any prop joint would need it and cannot be assumed

questions.question: Which replacement is actually playing, and how deep is the drop?
questions.have: 76 Out/Doubtful designations resolved against club depth charts; 39 replacements identified by name and chart tier.
questions.lack: An as-of date on most charts, and any official statement of who starts.
questions.answer: Tier is known for 39 of 76 absences. Of those, 34 are 2nd-stringers stepping in, 4 are 3rd-stringers and 1 is a 4th-stringer. The remaining 37 have no named replacement and are left blank rather than guessed.
questions.how_to_close: capture the as-of date with each chart; the join is already built

questions.question: How much is a starting-calibre absence actually worth in points?
questions.have: A positional cost table in the model and the absences that triggered it.
questions.lack: Any measurement. The costs are priors written by a previous session, not coefficients estimated from outcomes.
questions.answer: NOT ANSWERED, and this is the biggest single hole in the model. The injury adjustment moves lines by up to 6.5 points on the Week-10 slate on no measured basis.
questions.how_to_close: regress margin on absences x position once several seasons of designations and results are joined; needs more than one season

questions.question: How many bets before a real edge can be told apart from luck?
questions.have: An exact binomial power calculation, verified against enumeration.
questions.lack: Any settled, priced bets. The last published minimum of 300 was too low.
questions.answer: At -110, a true 55% bettor needs about 2272 settled bets for an 80%-power test. The previously published gate of 300 bets would only detect an edge of about 60%. A leaderboard populated sooner than this ranks noise, which is why it is empty and why it should stay empty.
questions.how_to_close: no shortcut exists; it is a waiting problem once prices exist

questions.question: Can a lucky staking run mask a bad signal?
questions.have: A measured demonstration under -110 prices with resampled orderings.
questions.lack: Nothing for the demonstration; real bet data would refine it.
questions.answer: Yes, easily, which is why signal and staking are separated: a strategy with a TRUE 45% rate still shows a profit after 100 bets 6.6% of the time. Separately, a 47% strategy outranks a 55% strategy 25.3% of the time over 20 bets. Ranking on bankroll is therefore inadmissible; the leaderboard ranks the signal first and prints staking second.
questions.how_to_close: closed; the rule is published in the gates

questions.question: Is home-field advantage big enough to price?
questions.have: A measured mean home margin of 0.469 points over 130 non-neutral finals.
questions.lack: Multi-season data. One season's interval is wide.
questions.answer: Not on this sample. 0.469 points with a 95% interval of -1.812 to 2.751 straddles zero, which is why the published model sets home-field to 0 and says so rather than assuming the usual 2.5-3 points. That is a defensible engineering choice and a genuinely surprising result that deserves the flag it carries.
questions.how_to_close: recompute after several seasons; a 3-point HFA would be visible

questions.question: Which margin values are dangerous to price a spread on?
questions.have: An empirical margin distribution over 137 finals.
questions.lack: Nothing here; this answer is complete for the sample.
questions.answer: Pushes cluster on the key numbers: 21.9% of games finish within 3 points and 51.8% within 7, so a line placed on 3 or 7 pushes far more often than a line placed on 1 or 12. Every originated spread is therefore checked against the key-number table before publication.
questions.how_to_close: closed for one season; refresh each season

questions.question: Are we permitted to publish lines, run a contest, and pay rewards?
questions.have: A statement of the question and a rule that nothing is paid.
questions.lack: Any legal review, any jurisdiction determined, any contest terms.
questions.answer: NOT ANSWERED and cannot be answered from data. This is a legal question that requires a person qualified to answer it. Until then the site publishes analysis, places no bets, and pays nothing.
questions.how_to_close: obtain review from a lawyer in the operating jurisdiction; no amount of modelling substitutes

questions.question: Is the injury adjustment even in the right direction from week to week?
questions.have: 13 originated lines with their injury deltas printed per game.
questions.lack: Enough games to test. One slate cannot test a coefficient.
questions.answer: UNKNOWN. The adjustment moves lines by up to 6.5 points, and no test of its sign exists. It is published as a DERIVED, uncalibrated input for exactly this reason.
questions.how_to_close: the same regression as Q-08; needs seasons, not weeks

suggestions.suggestion: Adopt the signal/staking split and the corrected minimum sample before any reward is offered.
suggestions.because: A 45% loser shows a profit after 100 bets 6.6% of the time, and the published 300-bet minimum detects only a ~60% edge. Ranking on bankroll or opening at 300 bets would pay luck.
suggestions.unlocks: a competition whose winner is meaningfully better, not luckier
suggestions.does_not: does not create a single settled bet; the board stays empty
suggestions.cost: 0 - the rules are computed in tools/decisions.py and tools/gates.py

suggestions.suggestion: License a price feed that publishes an open and a close per market, and write it through the existing snapshot store.
suggestions.because: Market values are the only thing separating a signal from an edge. Today all 39 market cells are blank. Every blocked gate (G-5, G-9) and every unanswerable market question depends on this one purchase.
suggestions.unlocks: CLV, ROI, the difference column, and gates G-5/G-9
suggestions.does_not: does not by itself validate anything; it supplies the missing input
suggestions.cost: a vendor contract; unknown price and terms

suggestions.suggestion: Estimate the injury and positional cost coefficients from outcomes instead of carrying written priors.
suggestions.because: The injury adjustment moves lines by up to 6.5 points with no measured basis (Q-08, Q-14). Until it is estimated, the largest single input to the board is an opinion.
suggestions.unlocks: a model whose biggest adjustment is measured
suggestions.does_not: does not help the total, which needs pace inputs instead (Q-03)
suggestions.cost: requires multiple seasons of designations joined to results

suggestions.suggestion: Investigate the measured home-field advantage of 0.469 points before accepting it as real.
suggestions.because: The interval [-1.812, 2.751] includes zero, which contradicts the conventional 2.5-3. If it is a small-sample artefact the model is under-adjusting; if it is real, that is a finding worth publishing. Either way the current choice to use zero is a decision that should be checked rather than inherited.
suggestions.does_not: does not require new data beyond more seasons

suggestions.suggestion: Replace the prose counts on the landing page with values rendered from the generated files.
suggestions.because: Prose counts drift: this repository has already published a wrong count once and a wrong arithmetic figure in this very session. Every number on the new pages is interpolated from data at build time, so a stale count fails the build instead of shipping.
suggestions.unlocks: a site where a wrong number cannot be published quietly
suggestions.does_not: does not fix numbers that are wrong in the source data

suggestions.suggestion: Capture an as-of date with every club depth chart, and drop charts that cannot be dated from any model input.
suggestions.because: 39 of 76 absences resolve to a named replacement, but most charts carry no as-of date and many clubs label them unofficial. An undated chart cannot be said to describe the week it is used for.
suggestions.unlocks: a depth layer that can support a model input
suggestions.does_not: does not make a club's chart an official statement of who starts

suggestions.suggestion: Publish the demotion gate's first firing as a news item, even when no strategy is live.
suggestions.because: A demotion rule that has never fired is untested. Exercising it on paper strategies, with the arithmetic shown, proves the mechanism works before it matters.
suggestions.unlocks: confidence that the rule is not decorative
suggestions.does_not: does not create live strategies to demote

suggestions.suggestion: Obtain legal review before publishing contest terms or a reward structure.
suggestions.because: Q-13 is unanswered and cannot be answered from data. Publishing a reward structure without review is the one action on this site that carries a risk no model can hedge.
suggestions.unlocks: the ability to run any contest at all
suggestions.does_not: nothing else on the site depends on it

method: Questions carry what we have, what we lack, the answer where the evidence supports one, and the specific step that would close it. Answers are only printed when a script in this repository measures them; a question with no measurable answer is left OPEN or BLOCKED rather than filled with reasoning.
